decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 1.25% to 1.5%. The vote was 9-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in November indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activ…”

changes.quote: Gains in employment, household spending, and business fixed investment have been solid, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has been expanding at a moderate rate, and growth in business fixed investment has picked up in recent quarters.”

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have continued to run below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined this year and are running below 2 percent.”

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation have increased in recent months but remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.”

changes.quote: Averaging through hurricane-related fluctuations, job gains have been solid, and the unemployment rate declined further.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace and labor market conditions will remain strong.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Consequently, the Committee continues to expect that, with gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pac…”

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run.
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate.
The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.08% APR costs about $54.50 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.72% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.04% would fall by about $1.73 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 172k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.1% over the past year (December 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.05%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.31% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 64%, cut 0%, hike 36%.

citations.detail: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent.
